transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, hello, Doctor. It’s a pleasure to meet you too. I really hope I'm not taking up too much of your busy schedule today. 

I'm mostly here because... well, my family and some friends have been saying I’ve been doing a bit too much lately. I certainly don't want to cause them any worry, so I agreed to come in and chat with you. I hope that's alright? 

Honestly, to me, it just feels like I’m the only one around with enough drive to actually get things done. We've got a move to handle, and I'm just making sure it goes smoothly. And I've been rebuilding the new garage—you know, just to make sure it’s done right. On top of that, I’ve been helping organize some things down at the church, and I'm still at the plant, showing the younger fellows on the mixing floor how a hard day's work really ought to be done. 

I just like being helpful and staying productive, you know? I hope that doesn't sound like a bad thing to you. Does that make sense?
Have you been needing less sleep than usual lately?

Well, I suppose I haven't been sleeping quite as much as I used to, but... I mean, that's just a normal part of getting older, isn't it? My father always said you sleep less when you have a full day ahead of you. 

I usually lay down for a few hours, maybe three or four, and then I'm just up and ready to go. I feel completely rested, I really do. It gives me a nice quiet time in the early morning to get a head start on the day's projects before anyone else is up to get underfoot. 

I don't think it's a problem, since I feel so full of energy. It's actually been quite nice, being so productive. Is that something I should be worried about, Doctor? I certainly don't want to be doing anything wrong.
Have you been feeling more confident or important than usual lately?

Well, gosh, I wouldn't say I feel more important than anybody else. I certainly don't want to come across as arrogant or boastful—that's just not how I was raised. 

I suppose I just feel... capable? Like I finally have the clarity and the energy to tackle things that maybe other folks find a bit overwhelming right now. Like with the young guys at the plant, I just know my experience is useful to them, and I want to share it. And with the church and the new garage... I just feel very sure of what needs to be done and how to do it right. 

It's just a good feeling of being useful, you know? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm full of myself. I really just want to be a help to everyone. Does that sound like a bad thing to you?
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Oh, heavens no. No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I mean, my hearing isn't quite what it used to be—too many years around the grinding machines at the plant, I suppose—but I certainly don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. 

I know sometimes folks my age can get a little confused, and I'd hate for you to think I'm losing my marbles or anything. My mind feels sharp as a tack, honestly. I'm just focused on getting my work done. That's perfectly normal, isn't it, Doctor? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Has this burst of energy been causing problems for you at work, at home, or with other people?

Well, I... I suppose there have been a few little hiccups, but nothing that can't be sorted out, really. I mean, I certainly didn't intend to cause any trouble for anyone. 

At the plant, there was a... a small misunderstanding about safety protocols. I was just trying to get things done faster, you know, show the younger fellas a more efficient way to run the grinders, but management felt I was moving a bit too fast. So, they asked me to step away for a bit. Just a temporary thing, I'm sure. I didn't want to upset them.

And at home... well, my wife and the kids have been a little worried, I guess. I had so many good ideas for the new garage and the move, and I was just trying to get the finances sorted to make it all happen, but they... they felt things were getting a little out of hand. They've asked me to hold off on making decisions about the money for now, and my wife even prefers to do the driving lately. 

I just wanted to help make everything perfect for them. I hate to think I've made them worry. It's not too unusual for families to have little disagreements like this when someone is just trying to do their best, right, Doctor? I hope you don't think poorly of me for it.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day?

Well, gosh... two whole weeks? I don't think so. I mean, everybody gets a little down in the dumps sometimes, don't they? Especially at my age, you know, when the weather turns cold or your joints are acting up. 

But depressed? No, I wouldn't use a strong word like that. I've always tried to look on the bright side and keep busy. If I ever feel a little blue, I just head out to the shed or try to find a little project to tinker with. I wouldn't want to be a burden on my wife by moping around the house all day. That's just not right, is it? 

I've always tried to be a good provider and keep a cheerful disposition for the family. So, no, I don't think I've ever had anything like what you're describing. That's a good thing, right, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the answers you need.
Before this recent high-energy period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt unusually energized like this?

Oh, heavens, no. No, I don't believe so. I've always been a hard worker, you know? Put in my time at the plant, did my best to provide for the family. But... well, this kind of energy, where I just don't need to sleep and my mind is racing with all these big plans... no, this is quite new to me. 

I've always been steady, reliable. I wouldn't want you to think I've spent my life running around causing a fuss or anything like that. I've always tried to be the kind of man people can count on. So, this is the first time I've felt quite this... revved up, I suppose you could say. That's helpful to know, isn't it, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of things.
How long has this unusually high-energy period been going on?

Well, let me think... I suppose it's been about a month now. Yes, right around the time we were forced to start packing up and leaving the old house. 

Moving is such a stressful thing, isn't it? Especially at my age. I just wanted to make sure everything was handled perfectly so my wife wouldn't have to worry about a single detail. I suppose that's why I've been pushing myself so hard lately, just trying to be helpful and get us settled. It's completely normal to get a little extra burst of energy when you're dealing with a big life change like that, don't you agree, Doctor? I just hope I haven't been overdoing it too much in my eagerness to help out.
At any other time in your life, have you ever had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Oh, um... well, like I mentioned just a little bit ago, I really don't think so. I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before, Doctor, I certainly don't want to make your job harder by making you ask twice! 

But no, even looking way back over my whole life... you know, when things were tough at the plant or money was tight... I never let myself get bogged down like that for weeks on end. It just wouldn't have been fair to my wife or the kids. I've always been the type to just pull my boots on and keep a smile on my face for them. 

So, no, never anything like that at any point. I hope that's okay? I really am trying to give you the best answers I can.
Before this past month, was there ever a time when your family or friends said you were acting unusually up or overly energetic, even if you didn’t see it that way?

Oh, my, no... no, I really don't think so. I mean, my wife, she's always said I'm a good provider and that I work hard, but... no, no one has ever told me I was acting strangely or overly energetic before this past month. 

I've always tried to be very mindful of how I come across to others, you see. I wouldn't want to be a bother or make anyone uncomfortable by acting out of sorts. I've just always tried to be the steady one. So, no, I've never had anyone pull me aside to say I was acting too "up" or anything like that. 

I hope I'm making sense, Doctor. I really want to be as helpful as possible for you. Does that answer your question all right?
